questions.text: Consider conventional CMOS ICs. A. Silicon is a semiconductor used in device regions. B. All interconnect layers must be electrically shorted together. C. Dielectrics separate conductors except at intended connections. Which statements are correct?
options: A only
A and C only
A, B and C
B and C only

questions.text: Two wires cross on insulated different layers with no via at the crossing. A. They need not be the same net. B. The crossing forces a DC short. C. Geometric separation proves zero capacitive coupling. Which statements are correct?
options: A and C only
A and B only
B and C only
A only

questions.text: Consider vias in an IC. A. They can connect selected metal layers. B. Their electrical and geometric properties matter in implementation. C. Adding a via automatically waives spacing rules. Which statements are correct?
options: A only
A and B only
B and C only
A, B and C

questions.text: What distinguishes a wafer from an individual die?
options: A die is the cylindrical silicon ingot before slicing.
A wafer usually contains many repeated die sites before dicing.
A wafer is the packaged form of a single die.
A die contains many separately packaged wafers.

questions.text: Under a simplified doubling-every-two-years transistor-count trend, what is the multiplication factor after six years?
Which statement about a CMOS inverter is appropriate for an introductory static model?
options: The pull-up and pull-down networks drive opposite output logic levels.
Its metal layers replace the need for transistors.
Its output always equals its input.
Its input is connected directly to both supply rails.

questions.text: What does a photomask specify in photolithography?
options: The measured defect count after packaging.
The software instructions run by a processor.
The spatial pattern used for an exposure step.
The RTL execution schedule of the complete circuit.

questions.text: Which ordering is consistent with a simplified subtractive pattern-transfer sequence?
options: Develop resist, expose, deposit film, strip resist, coat resist.
Etch all layers, coat resist, package, expose, develop.
Deposit film, coat resist, expose, develop, etch, strip resist.
Expose bare silicon, etch, coat resist, deposit film, develop.

questions.text: Why is using one unchanged mask for all patterned IC layers generally incorrect?
options: Different layers require different geometric patterns and alignment.
Every layer must contain exactly the same conductor shape.
Masks describe only package outlines.
Metal layers do not require pattern definition.

questions.text: Which statement correctly separates deposition from lithography?
options: Deposition converts RTL into gates; lithography selects software.
Lithography always deposits the final interconnect metal.
Both terms refer only to testing packaged chips.
Deposition adds material; lithography defines a pattern in resist.

questions.text: Which responsibility best matches a fabless company?
options: Supply only packaging without doing design.
Design chips while contracting wafer fabrication to a foundry.
Manufacture masks but never specify a circuit.
Operate every fabrication step in its own wafer plant.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of a process design kit (PDK)?
options: Replace the need to define the product function.
Guarantee that any RTL description is physically manufacturable.
Provide process-related rules, models and design data.
Contain only the finished packaged chip inventory.

questions.text: A low-volume prototype must be field-updated often and shipped quickly. Which implementation is usually the first candidate?
options: An untested bare wafer because it is reprogrammable.
FPGA, subject to its power and performance limits.
A standard-cell ASIC because it has no fixed development cost.
A new full-custom ASIC regardless of its schedule.

questions.text: What does a standard-cell design methodology reuse?
options: Pre-designed and characterized cells assembled into a custom circuit.
One fixed complete chip for every application.
A fabrication line that never uses custom interconnect masks.
Only a general-purpose CPU software instruction set.

questions.text: Which design style generally offers the greatest transistor-level customization?
options: A standard off-the-shelf FPGA bitstream.
Software-only implementation on a purchased CPU.
A fixed gate array with no interconnect customization.
Full-custom design.

questions.text: Compared with an ASIC implementation of the same function, an FPGA often has which cost pattern?
options: No unit cost because it is programmable.
Higher application-specific fixed cost and zero unit cost.
Lower application-specific fixed cost but higher unit cost.
Identical fixed and variable costs at every volume.

questions.text: For total cost C = F + N v, what does the slope with respect to production quantity N represent?
options: Variable cost per unit v.
The number of masks in the process.
The fixed development cost F.
The fraction of dies passing test.

questions.text: An ASIC costs 1,200,000 + 20N and an FPGA solution costs 200,000 + 70N, in the same units. At what quantity do the costs match?
options: 50,000 units
20,000 units
25,000 units
10,000 units

questions.text: Using C_ASIC=1,200,000+20N and C_FPGA=200,000+70N, which has lower modeled cost at N=10,000?
options: They both cost 1,400,000.
FPGA: 700,000 versus ASIC: 1,200,000.
ASIC: 400,000 versus FPGA: 900,000.
FPGA: 900,000 versus ASIC: 1,400,000.

questions.text: A wafer costs 6,000 units, has 500 gross dies and 80% die yield. Ignore all other costs. What is fabrication cost per good die?
options: 15 units
10 units
12 units
24 units

questions.text: An ASIC requires more fixed investment and has unit cost equal to its FPGA competitor. What happens in the simple linear cost model?
options: The ASIC becomes cheaper after exactly one unit.
There is no positive-volume break-even from unit-cost savings.
The two total costs are identical at every volume.
The larger fixed investment vanishes at high volume.

questions.text: If 350 out of 500 fabricated dies pass the stated tests, what is die yield?
Which comparison distinguishes power from energy?
options: A lower-power implementation always uses less task energy.
Energy per task depends on both average power and task duration.
Clock frequency alone determines both power and energy.
Power and energy have the same physical units.

questions.text: For unchanged activity, capacitance and frequency, voltage falls from 1.0 V to 0.8 V. In P_switch proportional to V squared, the power ratio is what?
Which design conclusion is justified by an increased clock frequency alone?
options: It always reduces the number of cycles per task.
It guarantees lower energy per completed task.
It proves smaller die area.
It reduces clock period, but end-to-end task latency also depends on cycle count.

questions.text: As a design moves from an algorithmic model toward physical layout, what generally happens?
options: Abstraction increases while geometry disappears.
All models contain exactly the same detail.
Exploration necessarily becomes faster at every later stage.
Abstraction decreases and implementation detail increases.

questions.text: Why can higher-level models help early design exploration?
options: They prove every physical signoff condition automatically.
They remove all need for functional specifications.
They omit lower-level detail so alternative architectures can be evaluated sooner.
They require completed mask data before simulation.

questions.text: Which function is usually a suitable candidate to remain in software?
options: A proven compute bottleneck needing fixed high-throughput arithmetic in every case.
The photoresist exposure step.
A control policy that must be updated frequently.
The mandatory physical connection between two metal layers.

questions.text: A computation takes 100 ms in software. Dedicated hardware needs 10 ms plus 30 ms transfer overhead. What is the end-to-end speedup?
options: 3.33 times
0.4 times
2.5 times
10 times

questions.text: Before accelerating a computation, why should transfer and coordination overhead be included?
options: They affect only the package color.
They are unrelated to latency.
They can reduce or eliminate the expected end-to-end speedup.
They are always zero when using dedicated hardware.

questions.text: What makes a system-on-chip (SoC) more than a collection of isolated verified IP blocks?
options: The integrated system also needs compatible interfaces and system-level verification.
Every block must be rewritten from scratch.
Top-level verification becomes unnecessary after vendor verification.
No block may be reused.

questions.text: Which statement distinguishes soft IP from hard IP in a common usage?
options: Soft IP is typically supplied as synthesizable RTL; hard IP as a process-specific physical implementation.
Soft IP contains no functional behavior.
Hard IP can never contain a memory.
Both necessarily have identical process portability.

questions.text: An IP block has a different reset convention and clock domain from its new host. What is required?
options: Assume the vendor verified every possible host environment.
Remove all registers from the IP.
Resolve the integration assumptions and verify the interface behavior.
Connect the ports by name and omit further checks.

questions.text: Which item is useful IP integration metadata?
options: Only a screenshot of the completed chip package.
Interface timing, protocol, clock/reset and configuration requirements.
Only the number of staff employed by the vendor.
Only the marketing name of the block.

questions.text: What is behavioural synthesis, also called high-level synthesis (HLS)?
options: Constructing a timed RTL architecture from an algorithmic description under constraints.
Executing a C program only on a general-purpose CPU.
Drawing final transistor polygons directly from an SDC file.
Converting a packaged chip back into a silicon ingot.

questions.text: Which decision belongs to HLS scheduling?
options: Assign operations to clock steps while respecting dependencies and constraints.
Measure wafer yield after manufacturing.
Choose the final chip package color.
Assign every net to a detailed routing track.

questions.text: Which decision belongs to HLS resource binding?
options: Choose which lithography mask is exposed first.
Compute final layout-vs-schematic equivalence from polygons.
Specify only the total production volume.
Associate scheduled operations with particular hardware resources.

questions.text: In HLS terminology, what does resource allocation determine?
options: The physical routing layer of every signal.
Only which die passes a manufacturing test.
Only the final names of input variables.
The types and numbers of resources made available to the architecture.

questions.text: A computation needs two additions. One nonpipelined adder can perform one addition per cycle. Ignoring other limits, what resource lower bound applies to its steady-state initiation interval?
options: At least 2 cycles per transaction.
At most half a cycle.
Exactly 1 cycle because the expression has one result.
Zero cycles if the RTL is automatically generated.

questions.text: A two-stage pipeline runs at a 10 ns period and accepts a new independent item every cycle. What are its ideal latency and initiation interval in time?
options: 10 ns latency and 20 ns initiation interval.
10 ns latency and zero initiation interval.
20 ns latency and 10 ns initiation interval.
20 ns latency and 20 ns initiation interval necessarily.

questions.text: A pipeline has a 5 ns clock and an initiation interval of 2 cycles. What is its ideal steady-state throughput?
options: 200 million items per second
10 million items per second
100 million items per second
400 million items per second

questions.text: What can resource sharing in HLS change?
options: Area, operand selection, storage/control needs and the acceptance schedule.
The need for any clocked storage always disappears.
Only variable spelling, with no architectural effect.
Only fabrication yield, never timing.

questions.text: Which is an advantage of HLS when used with suitable code and constraints?
options: It can explore different RTL architectures from one high-level function.
It accepts every operating-system call as hardware.
It eliminates all RTL and system verification.
It guarantees the best possible PPA for every algorithm.

questions.text: Which limitation should be considered before using an HLS tool?
options: Only a supported synthesizable language subset maps to finite hardware resources.
All loop bounds and data dependencies are irrelevant.
Any arbitrary host operating-system operation becomes a hardware port automatically.
The generated circuit can dynamically acquire unlimited physical memory.

questions.text: A pipelined implementation computes (a+b)+c from successive input transactions. Why may c need a matching delay register?
options: To force every transaction to have identical input values.
To eliminate the second addition mathematically.
To convert the entire design into software.
To align c with the partial sum from the same transaction.

questions.text: A shell is currently in /home/k/lab. What path does ../rtl/top.v refer to?
options: /rtl/top.v
/home/rtl/top.v
/home/k/lab/rtl/top.v
/home/k/rtl/top.v

questions.text: Consider touch under normal Unix permissions. A. It can create a file if absent. B. It normally erases an existing file. C. It can update timestamps while preserving existing contents. Which statements are correct?
options: A and C only
A and B only
A, B and C
B only

questions.text: Consider common Unix commands. A. ls -a includes dot-prefixed entries. B. df primarily lists shell job numbers. C. du can report directory disk usage. Which statements are correct?
options: B and C only
A, B and C
A only
A and C only

questions.text: What distinguishes Ctrl+Z followed by bg from terminating a foreground job?
options: The operating system is put to sleep.
The job is suspended and then resumed in the background.
The process is permanently deleted from disk.
The command is rerun from its beginning with a new input file.

questions.text: Which pairing is correct for common Unix tools?
options: df lists shell job numbers; du lists register names.
du reports clock period; df reports gate delay.
du reports directory disk usage; df reports filesystem space.
du and df both change file ownership.
